::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
**Please do not pick one of these.**

They exist so that nobody is stuck staring at a blank page in week 2.
Every one is a lead, not a project. Each still has to survive the
[feasibility filter](sessions/01-introductions.qmd), and each still needs a
decision attached to it before it is worth doing.

The best capstones have always come from somebody's own curiosity. If
one of these sparks a better idea two steps sideways, that is what it is
for.
:::

Where each dataset lives, and how to get an account, is on the
[data sources](data-sources.qmd) page. Methods for generating your own
ideas are in [meeting 1](sessions/01-introductions.qmd).

Archetypes: **1** evaluation · **2** preference & pricing ·
**3** prediction & risk · **4** diagnosis · **5** feasibility.

## Property and place

| | The lead | Data | Type |
|--:|:--|:--|:--|
| 1 | What is a water view worth, and does the premium survive when you compare near-identical houses? | ATTOM transactions + Nature Score (Dewey) | 2 |
| 2 | Is flood or fire risk discounted in house prices yet — and did that change after a local disaster? | US Climate Risk × ATTOM (Dewey) | 1 |
| 3 | When a housing market softens, which price tier moves first? | ATTOM + Dwellsy rents (Dewey) | 4 |
| 4 | Can you beat "last sale price, index-adjusted" at valuing a listing — and what are the big misses? | ATTOM (Dewey) | 3 |
| 5 | Where do people move after a mass layoff in their county? | Consumer Address History × WARN (Dewey) | 4 |

## Collect it yourself

Ideas 15, 28 and anything like them need no dataset at all. You write the
instrument and field it.

This is worth taking seriously. The most ambitious project in this
programme's history ran online experiments on brand recognition, then
persuaded a soda company to donate thousands of cans for a field
experiment in dining halls. That was a nine-month MPS team. It took no
econometrics.

Meeting 9 teaches instrument design and how large a sample you need.
[Permissions and ethics](permissions.qmd) covers the IRB, and you should
start that in October.

## If none of these fit

Good. Bring your own.

Take it to the four filter questions from meeting 1. Could a team of 3–5
execute it in one spring semester? Can you name the data, who holds it,
and how you get it — checked, not assumed? Could the answer come out
either way? Would anybody act differently depending on it?

Survives all four? Label its archetype and bring it to class. Fails one?
Say which. A question you kill in September is a month you do not lose in
March.
